claims.text: A machine-learning predictive approach will outperform analytical methods in estimating the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed approach can predict lattice thermal conductivity without conflating it with electronic thermal conductivity.
The approach will remain effective across a temperature range extending from 10 K to 1200 K.
The approach will be particularly advantageous below 200 K and above 300 K.
The modeled material is HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
The machine-learning model will be trained using DFT-derived elastic properties, Debye temperatures, and experimental data.
Defect scattering and anharmonic phonon interactions are relevant structural or transport mediators for the alloy's lattice thermal conductivity.
The model will integrate defect-induced scattering and anharmonic phonon effects.
Analytical methods do not fully capture defect-induced scattering and anharmonic phonon effects.
Accounting for defect scattering and anharmonic phonon effects will make lattice-thermal-conductivity predictions more accurate in oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr.
The model's lattice thermal conductivity predictions will be within ±10% of experimental measurements over the specified temperature range.
The analytical baseline uses perfect-crystal assumptions and simplified phonon-transport models.
The hypothesis is applicable to HfNbTaTiZr alloys with oxygen impurity levels similar to 1 wt.%.
The approach may not generalize to alloys with substantially different compositions or impurity levels.
Prediction uncertainty depends on the availability and quality of training data and on the model's ability to represent relevant atomic-scale interactions.
